scenes.text: How does a repository reach your service?
scenes.phonemes: hˌaʊ dˈʌz ɐ ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi ɹˈiːtʃ jʊɹ sˈɜːvɪs?

scenes.text: Configured scanning finds annotated classes and registers bean definitions.
scenes.phonemes: kənfˈɪɡɚd skˈænɪŋ fˈaɪndz ˈænətˌeɪɾᵻd klˈæsᵻz ænd ɹˈɛdʒɪstɚz bˈiːn dˌɛfɪnˈɪʃənz.

scenes.text: A single constructor needs a repository. Spring resolves that parameter by type.
scenes.phonemes: ɐ sˈɪŋɡəl kənstɹˈʌktɚ nˈiːdz ɐ ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi. spɹˈɪŋ ɹᵻzˈɑːlvz ðæt pɚɹˈæmɪɾɚ baɪ tˈaɪp.

scenes.text: Spring creates the repository, then passes its reference into the service constructor.
scenes.phonemes: spɹˈɪŋ kɹiːˈeɪts ðə ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi, ðˈɛn pˈæsᵻz ɪts ɹˈɛfɹəns ˌɪntʊ ðə sˈɜːvɪs kənstɹˈʌktɚ.

scenes.text: Our Java run confirms the same repository bean. Only then does the application use the service.
scenes.phonemes: ˌaʊɚ dʒˈɑːvɚ ɹˈʌn kənfˈɜːmz ðə sˈeɪm ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi bˈiːn. ˈoʊnli ðˈɛn dˈʌz ðɪ ˌæplɪkˈeɪʃən jˈuːs ðə sˈɜːvɪs.

scenes.text: Scan, register, resolve, inject, then use. Spring supplies dependencies; your service doesn’t construct them.
scenes.phonemes: skˈæn, ɹˈɛdʒɪstɚ, ɹᵻzˈɑːlv, ɪndʒˈɛkt, ðˈɛn jˈuːz. spɹˈɪŋ səplˈaɪz dᵻpˈɛndənsiz; jʊɹ sˈɜːvɪs dˈʌzənt kənstɹˈʌkt ðˌɛm.
